title: Best Payroll Software 2026
description: Top 5 payroll software picks for 2026: Gusto (4.5/5, $40/mo + $6/person) leads the ranking for companies running payroll across states and countries. Compare ratings, pricing, and user feedback across 5 verified picks.

pros: Fully automated payroll with tax filings calculated, filed, and paid automatically on every payroll run with zero manual intervention
New hire onboarding that auto-populates federal and state tax forms, sends e-signature requests, and creates employee accounts
Health insurance administration with multi-carrier comparison shopping, enrollment management, and ACA compliance reporting
cons: Limited to US customers only with no international payroll support, excluding growing remote teams with global hires
Time tracking and PTO management features feel basic compared to dedicated HR platforms like BambooHR
picks.bestFor: Best for gusto is ideal for small to mid-size teams that need a reliable hr & people solution without excessive complexity

pros: Unified HR-IT-Finance platform eliminates manual cross-department handoffs — a single employee hire action automatically creates payroll records, provisions devices, grants app access, and enrolls benefits, reducing onboarding time by 60-80%
App provisioning automation (SSO identity provider + device MDM) enables policy-driven access management for 500+ apps including Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, and Salesforce

Device management with mobile device management (MDM) for Mac, Windows, and Linux — remotely wipe, lock, or configure company devices, enforce disk encryption, and deploy software from the same platform that manages employee records
cons: Pricing is higher per user than standalone HRIS platforms — Rippling starts at $8/user/month for HR + payroll + IT, while BambooHR or Gusto provide basic HR at $5-6/user/month with fewer unified features

Implementation complexity for the IT and finance modules is higher than standalone HRIS — configuring SSO, MDM profiles, app integrations, and spend policies requires dedicated IT administration time beyond standard HR configuration
picks.bestFor: Best for fast-growing startups that need a scalable hr & people platform

pros: Global contractor management in 150+ countries with local compliance
EOR hiring eliminating entity setup costs for international expansion
Automated payroll with multi-currency and multi-country runs
cons: $49/contractor/month minimum pricing for core EOR service
Full EOR costs $599/month per employee vs local entity payroll
picks.bestFor: Best for deel is ideal for small to mid-size teams that need a reliable hr & payroll solution without excessive complexity

pros: Intuitive interface with a 4.5/5 user satisfaction rating on G2, reducing HR admin onboarding time by approximately 60% compared to traditional HRIS systems based on customer-reported implementation timelines

Time-off tracking automates accrual rule calculation for vacation, sick, and personal days across 50+ configurable policies with carryover, caps, and proration, eliminating manual spreadsheet tracking

Applicant tracking system integrates job posting, candidate screening, interview scheduling, offer letters, and e-signatures into a single pipeline, reducing average time-to-hire by 7-10 days compared to disconnected tools
cons: Payroll is available only for US-based companies and lacks support for complex pay structures such as multi-state tax handling, union deductions, and prevailing wage calculations that mid-market competitors offer

Performance management module lacks 360-degree feedback, OKR/goal alignment, and continuous feedback features present in dedicated platforms like Lattice or Culture Amp, limiting its value for performance-driven cultures
picks.bestFor: Best for bambooHR is perfect for freelancers and independent professionals who need an affordable, easy-to-use hr & people tool

pros: Compliance infrastructure is the deepest in the industry — handles multi-state payroll tax filing, garnishment processing, FMLA/leave administration, union contract compliance, and ACA/COBRA reporting across all 50 states automatically

Global payroll coverage in 140+ countries through ADP GlobalView or Celergo provides unified payroll processing for multinational organizations without maintaining separate payroll providers per country

Garnishment and wage attachment processing is automated — ADP receives electronic court orders, calculates deductions per state law, processes payments, and manages compliance documentation for child support, tax levies, and creditor garnishments
cons: User interface lags modern HRIS platforms significantly — the Workforce Now interface uses dated design patterns, dense data layouts, and navigation structures that require 20-40 hours of training for administrators to navigate efficiently

Implementation timelines are long (3-9 months) and complex, requiring dedicated project management resources, parallel payroll runs, and extensive data migration planning that smaller platforms complete in weeks
